headline: FRIEDLAND'S IVANHOE ELECTRIC DRILLS 123.6m AT 0.91% COPPER AT GLEESON ARIZONA — High-Grade Breccia Discovery 28 Miles North of Bisbee; Ranked Top Exploration Project
snippet: Ivanhoe Electric (NYSE: IE) announced on November 19 its first drill holes at the Gleeson copper-gold-silver project in southeastern Arizona returned 123.60 metres at 0.91% copper, 0.44 g/t gold and 5.27 g/t silver from 601.70m depth — including a higher-grade sub-interval of 1.38% copper over 71.03m — confirming breccia and carbonate-hosted copper-gold-silver mineralization the company now ranks as its top exploration project. Located 28 miles north of the historic Bisbee copper district, the discovery is open in multiple directions, two rigs are actively drilling and the company targets 16,000 metres of drilling by year-end, adding a significant new Arizona copper discovery to the portfolio of Robert Friedland-linked Ivanhoe Electric alongside its advanced Santa Cruz project.

headline: GOLD'S BIGGEST DAILY PLUNGE SINCE COVID — Are Miners Still a Buy? GDX -9.4%, GDXJ -10.4% as Sector Braces for More
snippet: Stockhead's market analysis of November 20 examines whether today's gold price crash — the metal's largest single-session percentage drop since the COVID-era 2020 selloff — creates a genuine buy opportunity for mining equities, with the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) falling 9.4% and the junior GDXJ declining 10.4% as the sector amplified gold's move. The analysis highlights the persistent pattern of miners falling two to three times harder than the underlying metal in this correction cycle, and poses the question experienced gold investors are asking: whether the extreme miner-versus-metal disconnect, with P/NAV ratios at decade lows, represents a generational accumulation window or simply confirms that financial conditions will remain hostile to mining equities until the Fed's rate cycle clearly turns.

headline: ASX GOLD MINERS LEAD LOSSES FOR SECOND STRAIGHT DAY — Northern Star, Evolution, Genesis Down 8-10% as Bullion Rout Extends
snippet: Australian gold miners dominated the worst-performing sector on the ASX 200 for the second consecutive session on November 20 as the spot gold price correction deepened through multi-month lows, with Northern Star Resources, Evolution Mining and Genesis Minerals all falling 8-10% — losses that reflect both the commodity price move and the sector's amplified leverage to gold in a rising-rate, strong-dollar environment. For ASX investors, the two-day selloff has erased months of outperformance built on Australian dollar gold price strength, and the index-level impact is significant given gold miners comprise over 15% of the ASX 200 materials sector; the question of whether this is temporary deleveraging or the start of a structural re-rating lower is the central debate for portfolio managers heading into the final weeks of 2026.

headline: NICKEL CREEK PLATINUM HALTS 2026 YUKON DRILL PROGRAM — Cash Constraints, Bad Weather and Poor Ground Conditions Stop Program Before Target Depth
snippet: Nickel Creek Platinum (TSX-V: NCP) announced November 19 it is halting its 2026 drill program at the Wellgreen target within the Nickel Shäw Project in Yukon after two holes failed to reach the 600-metre target depth — the first abandoned for unfavourable ground conditions and the second stopped for weather and safety reasons before entering the target zone. The company left casing in place for a potential re-entry, but CEO Stuart Harshaw acknowledged additional financing will be required to continue drilling — a candid disclosure from a company that raised only $655,000 in its October 2026 placement and has yet to test the deep target that the project thesis depends on.

headline: EPIC GOLD ANNOUNCES INITIAL 279,000 OZ RESOURCE AT WILSON QUEBEC — 3.047Mt at 2.85 g/t Au; Second Quebec Resource Adds to 440K Oz Hawkins Ontario
snippet: EPIC Gold Corp (CSE: EPG) released an initial inferred mineral resource estimate for its Wilson Gold Project in Québec on November 19, outlining 3.047 million tonnes grading 2.85 g/t Au for 279,000 ounces — adding a second Quebec resource to the company's growing portfolio following the separate 440,400-ounce inferred estimate at its Hawkins project in Ontario reported in October 2026. At 2.85 g/t, Wilson's grade is well above the TSX-V average for bulk-tonnage gold resources, and together with Fenton and Hawkins, EPIC's total ounce count across properties is now approaching 800,000 ounces — building a multi-asset platform that positions the company for a larger-scale resource consolidation story at a time when high-grade Quebec gold developers are attracting consolidation interest from mid-tier producers.

headline: GOLD EXTENDS LOSSES ON TIGHTER FED OUTLOOK — Saxo's Hansen Flags ETF Liquidation Risk; $3,500 May Not Hold
snippet: Saxo Bank's Ole Sloth Hansen warned that elevated gold-backed ETF holdings leave the market vulnerable to continued liquidation as a December Fed rate hike prints at over 90% probability, adding that profit-taking from investors who bought gold below $4,000 is compounding the financial-driven selling pressure — a concern that the $3,500 structural support, while expected to attract central bank buying, may not hold if forced liquidation from leveraged products accelerates before year-end. Hansen's framing reflects the current market dilemma: the fundamental case for gold remains intact, but the financial conditions that broke gold below $4,000 show no sign of reversing in the near term.

headline: INVESTING.COM: GOLD BREAKDOWN BELOW $3,700 SIGNALS DEEPER RATE-DRIVEN SELLOFF — December FOMC Now the Key Pivot Point
snippet: An Investing.com technical and macro analysis flags gold's breach of $3,700 as a structurally significant breakdown that signals further downside unless financial conditions shift materially, attributing the move primarily to a strengthening US dollar and rising real yields driven by hawkish Fed expectations rather than any change in physical demand or geopolitical fundamentals. The analysis pinpoints December's FOMC meeting as the critical inflection: a sell-the-news reaction to a priced-in rate hike could mark the correction low, while a more-hawkish-than-expected meeting or statement could send gold toward the mid-$3,000 range before year-end buyers emerge in force.

headline: ALL SIX PRECIOUS METALS ETFs BROKEN BELOW 100-WEEK EMA — GDX, GDXJ, SIL, SILJ, GLD, SLV in Technical Breakdown; 'No Floor in Sight' Yet
snippet: SilverGoldAlpha's November 20 analysis confirms all six major precious metals and mining ETFs — GDX, GDXJ, SIL, SILJ, GLD and SLV — have broken below their 100-week exponential moving averages simultaneously, a rare alignment that the author says has occurred only three times in the past decade and each time preceded either a significant further decline or a sharp reversal within four to six weeks. The technical breakdown removes a key support level that has historically acted as a valuation floor for institutional investors using long-term trend-following models, and the note argues that until these averages are reclaimed, the burden of proof is on the bulls to identify a catalyst — whether a Fed pivot signal, a geopolitical safe-haven spike, or a dollar reversal — rather than relying on mean-reversion alone.

headline: GOLD, SILVER AND MINING STOCKS DISCONNECT FROM NVIDIA — Why Metals Sold Off Harder Than Tech on the Same Day
snippet: BullionVault's November 17 market commentary examines the unusual session in which gold, silver and mining stocks declined significantly while NVIDIA rallied and Deutsche Bank reversed course — a divergence that challenges the simplistic 'inflation hedge' framing of precious metals and reveals that the current selloff is being driven by financial conditions (rising real yields and a strong dollar) rather than a retreat in inflation expectations or risk appetite broadly. The piece argues that the metals-tech divergence actually reinforces the structural bull case: when AI-driven tech spending revives, the copper and critical minerals embedded in that infrastructure buildout will see demand that financial market volatility cannot permanently suppress.

headline: SCHRODERS SEES 'VERY SHARP YEAR-END GOLD RALLY' AS CTAs GO RECORD SHORT — Energy Headwind Fading; Physical Buyers Waiting at $3,500
snippet: Schroders' ISF Global Gold fund analysts told Kitco on November 16 that commodity trading advisers have built some of the largest short positions on record in gold futures, creating the conditions for a potentially violent year-end rally if any catalyst shifts sentiment — including an energy price pullback, a softer-than-expected December CPI, or a Fed statement that leaves room for 2027 rate cuts. While elevated energy prices have been Schroders' primary explanation for why gold has failed to hold above $4,000 this year, the analysts say the structural demand case — from central bank diversification, geopolitical safe-haven buying and de-dollarisation flows — remains fully intact, and that the current correction represents a positioning flush rather than a fundamental shift in gold's multi-year bull market thesis.
